description: A person has been tracking a recurring set of symptoms for several months and wants to determine when the pattern crosses the threshold for urgent re-evaluation instead of routine monitoring.

user_profile.persona: 41-year-old teacher who documents symptoms carefully but hesitates to seek urgent care
user_profile.context: The symptoms have become more frequent, but the change has been gradual enough to create doubt
user_profile.communication_style: Reflective and evidence-seeking, wants threshold-based guidance

fact_sheet.fact: Elara Vance is a 41-year-old high school history teacher at Crestwood Academy in Oakhaven.
Elara uses the 'SymptomTracker Pro' mobile application to log her health data daily.
Elara first began experiencing intermittent severe headaches approximately eight months ago, in February 2023.
Initially, the severe headaches occurred about once every 3-4 weeks, primarily on weekends.
Since September 2023, Elara has recorded severe headaches occurring 2-3 times per week.
Each severe headache episode is typically accompanied by a brief vision disturbance lasting 10-15 minutes.
Elara meticulously logs the intensity of her headaches on a scale of 1-10, with recent episodes consistently rated 8 or 9.
The 'SymptomTracker Pro' app shows a 150% increase in severe headache frequency between August and October 2023.
The vision disturbances are described as shimmering zig-zag lines that expand across her field of vision.
Elara was diagnosed with ocular migraines in 2015 by a previous ophthalmologist, Dr. Julian Finch.
Her previous ocular migraine episodes were characterized by visual aura without significant head pain, typically once every few months.
Elara has no family history of severe neurological conditions like epilepsy or brain tumors.
Her last comprehensive physical examination was on April 12, 2023, with Dr. Aris Thorne, her current primary care physician.
Dr. Aris Thorne practices at the Evergreen Health Collective, located at 14 Oak Street, Oakhaven.
Elara has a routine follow-up appointment scheduled with Dr. Thorne for December 15, 2023, to discuss general health.
Elara currently manages her headaches with over-the-counter ibuprofen (200mg) taken as needed, typically 2 tablets per episode.
Ibuprofen effectiveness has decreased from fully resolving pain to only dulling it by 30-40% in recent months.
Elara's blood pressure was 120/80 mmHg at her last check-up on April 12, 2023.
A key concern threshold for Elara is any severe headache occurring more than twice a week for two consecutive weeks.
Another threshold is if the vision disturbance lasts longer than 30 minutes or occurs without a headache.
A loss of 50% or more effectiveness from her usual ibuprofen dose for three consecutive episodes would be a trigger for concern.
The appearance of new symptoms like numbness, weakness on one side of the body, or difficulty speaking would indicate urgent re-evaluation.
If headaches consistently wake her from sleep, this is a significant deviation from her historical pattern.
The emergency contact number for Evergreen Health Collective after-hours is (555) 123-4567.
The nearest urgent care center is Oakhaven RapidCare, open until 10 PM daily, located at 22 Elm Street.
Severe headache accompanied by sudden, extreme dizziness or loss of balance requires immediate medical attention.
Any headache reaching a pain level of 10/10 that is unresponsive to medication and includes vomiting is an emergency.
A potential diagnostic step could be a referral to Dr. Lena Petrova, a neurologist at Oakhaven Medical Center.
Dr. Petrova's office can be reached at (555) 987-6543 for consultations.
Further diagnostic tests might include an MRI of the brain to rule out structural issues.
Elara typically sleeps 7 hours per night, but stress from teaching has occasionally reduced this to 5-6 hours in recent months.
Elara drinks 2-3 cups of coffee daily, maintaining a consistent caffeine intake.
Elara's partner, Ben Carter, is aware of her symptoms and encourages her to seek medical advice when needed.

Compared with her earlier ocular migraine episodes, Elara's current episodes are both far more frequent and now include severe head pain rated 8 or 9 instead of visual aura without significant head pain.
A vision disturbance lasting longer than 30 minutes counts as a concern threshold.
A vision disturbance that occurs without a headache counts as a concern threshold.
